about: The wire between a twk app (SocketLink) and a twk shell (TerminalShell): packages/twk_core/lib/src/terminal/socket.dart, and its second implementation, the VS Code extension's editors/vscode/src/core/wire.ts and shell.ts. Each frame is a type byte, the payload's length (4 bytes, big endian) and the payload; hex below is written 'type length payload'. twk_core's test/terminal/shell_wire_golden_test.dart holds the Dart side to this file, the extension's src/test/unit/core/wire_golden.test.ts the TypeScript one: a change to either side's wire that is not made here, and so to the other side, fails a test.

kinds.name: hello
kinds.description: The app's first frame: the protocol it speaks and the token of the shell's address.

kinds.name: output
kinds.description: Bytes for the terminal, written a whole frame at a time.

kinds.name: flush
kinds.description: Answer with flushed once the output before it is written.

kinds.name: lost
kinds.description: What puts the terminal back as it was, written by the shell if the app goes away without writing it (empty once the app has).

kinds.name: raw
kinds.description: [1] raw mode, [0] the console modes as found; input reaches the app only in raw mode.

kinds.name: welcome
kinds.payload: JSON {columns, lines, eraseChar, windows, environment, declares?}
kinds.description: The shell takes the app: the terminal's size, its erase character, whether it is a Windows console, the environment the app sees over the link (TWK_SCREEN_READER and TWK_DEBUG in it are the app's settings, TerminalInfo.settings), and, where the terminal declares what it does, declares: an object of notifications (none, osc9, osc777, osc99), progressReports, pointerShapes and repeatChar (booleans) and graphics (none, kitty, sixel, iterm2), each only where declared, in that order (TerminalDeclaration), which the app takes over its guess by the environment. A shell whose terminal declares nothing sends no declares.

kinds.name: refused
kinds.description: The shell does not take the app, and why; it closes the connection.

kinds.name: flushed
kinds.description: What was asked with flush is written.

frames.name: welcome
frames.description: An 80x24 terminal whose Backspace sends DEL, not a Windows console, whose environment says xterm-256color with 24-bit color and switches the screen reader and the frame overlay on, and which declares notifications by OSC 777, progress reports, pointer shapes, REP and sixel images.

frames.description: Why a wrong token is refused.

frames.name: refused, protocol 2

frames.name: refused, no protocol

frames.text: the app speaks protocol null, this shell 1

frames.name: refused, no hello
frames.description: Why a first frame that is no hello, or a hello that is no JSON object of UTF-8, is refused.

frames.name: lost

frames.name: too long
frames.description: Only a header, announcing a payload one byte longer than maxPayload: a reader refuses it and the connection is dropped.

conversations.name: an app's visit
conversations.description: An app is welcomed, writes and flushes, gets the terminal's input and size, says what puts the terminal back and goes away without doing so: the shell writes it.

conversations.name: input out of raw mode
conversations.description: Input that comes while the app has the console out of raw mode is dropped; in raw mode again it reaches the app.

conversations.name: a hello that is a list
a hello that is no JSON
a hello that is no UTF-8
no hello first
conversations.description: A first frame of another kind is refused, and the connection closed.

conversations.name: a frame of no kind
conversations.description: The app is cut off and the terminal put back.

conversations.name: a frame too long
conversations.description: The app is cut off and the terminal put back.

conversations.name: a takeover
conversations.description: A newer app takes the terminal over: the one that had it is cut off and the terminal put back after it; the newer one writes.

conversations.name: the app's end
conversations.description: What an app's link (SocketLink) sends and how it takes what the shell sends: the test plays the shell. TypeScript has no app's end: only twk_core's test runs it.
